title: Fats's recording group: Sedric replaces Whitted; substitutes Hamilton and Coleman
summary: The group stayed the same except Eugene Sedric came in for Whitted after the first date; Autrey missed only a few dates, when Johnny Hamilton or Bill Coleman took his place.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did the group change from date to date?
No, we stuck there. Let me see, we had the same group, Herman Autrey on trumpet; the guitar, same; bass player, same; Eugene Sedric, the same;
You've got Sedric now, because before
you had -- you said you had Whitted in the first band.

Oh, Whitted. Oh that's -- after the first date -- now just a second. There was no Whitted. Eugene Sedric came in, because I did know the reason why, because Sedric came out and had something to do with a date, another date that we had, and they brought in Eugene Sedric. Truthfully, right now I can't think, but there is a particular reason, and it wasn't -- uh -- nothing inferior, I would say, I mean about --

-- about Whitted, no. Whitted is a heck of a nice guy, and we loved him. Fats enjoyed his work, and all that. I'm trying to think now how Sedric got in there, and I do know, and I'm trying to think of it. But from there, that Sedric got in, that was it, you know? Uh-huh.
Had Sedric worked with Fats before?
I see. He didn't know -- what had he been doing at that time?
Ah, well Sedric -- Eugene Sedric had been to Europe with -- uh -- I'm trying to think of the big band. He'd been to -- he'd been to Europe.
Yeah, with a big band. A big -- a very -- big name, too. Very nice guy, a very fine man. But

I didn't know Sedric then, while he was with this band. I don't think Fats did either. But I found out later, he had been to Europe with this group, you know. And -- a year, and had been back, you know. And no, oh man, I can't think.
That's okay. Now how long did the -- did you play on all of Fats's dates?
At the beginning? I mean there were some later on that you weren't on.

I did -- the only ones I did not do was when I was sick with a cold, or something. John Hamilton, "Buggs" Johnny Burks, took my place, and another time I didn't show up, Bill Coleman did a date for me. A very fine trumpet player, both these guys, terrific. Bill Coleman and Johnny "Buggs", or John Hamilton, whichever is the preferred, you know?
